before.name: Comparing Time Durations
before.description: Compare durations of events and calculate the time taken by particular events or tasks
evidence: Work out that a TV show from 5:17 p.m. to 5:43 p.m. lasted 26 minutes
Compare a 35-minute bus journey with a 40-minute walk and say which takes longer and by how much
Solve 'The lesson starts at 10:15 and ends at 11:00. How long is it?' (45 minutes)
before.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} starts cooking at 4:15 p.m. and finishes at 5:00 p.m., can they work out how long the cooking took?

after.name: Calculating elapsed duration
after.description: Calculate the duration between a known start time and a known finish time, including across an hour boundary; distinguish the interval length from either clock reading.
evidence: Work out that a TV show from 5:17 p.m. to 5:43 p.m. lasted 26 minutes
Find that an activity from 2:50 p.m. to 4:10 p.m. lasts 1 hour 20 minutes, explaining the regrouping at 60 minutes
Solve a lesson from 10:15 to 11:00 as a duration of 45 minutes, using a number line or another valid method
after.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} starts cooking at 4:15 p.m. and finishes at 5:00 p.m., can they work out how long it took and explain how they know?

before.name: Elapsed time problems
before.description: Solve word problems involving elapsed time by adding and subtracting time intervals in minutes, including using a number line
evidence: A film starts at 2:15 and lasts 47 minutes — when does it end?
Calculate how many minutes between 9:20 and 10:05
Use a number line to show the elapsed time between two events
before.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} starts football practice at 3:20 p.m. and it lasts 75 minutes, can they work out what time it finishes — using a number line to help?

after.name: Finding start or finish times
after.description: Find an unknown start or finish time from a given duration and the other clock time. Choose whether to move forwards or backwards, regrouping minutes at 60 when crossing an hour; a number line is one useful representation.
evidence: A film starts at 2:15 p.m. and lasts 47 minutes: find its finish time of 3:02 p.m.
A show ends at 10:05 a.m. and lasts 45 minutes: find its start time of 9:20 a.m.
Explain why a known start and duration require moving forwards, while a known finish and duration require moving backwards; check the result against the story
after.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} starts football practice at 3:20 p.m. and it lasts 75 minutes, can they find the finish time? If another practice finishes at 5:10 p.m. after 45 minutes, can they find when it started and explain the different directions?

before.name: Time to the nearest minute
before.description: Tell, write and estimate the time to the nearest minute on analogue and digital clocks, using vocabulary such as o'clock, a.m./p.m., morning, afternoon, noon and midnight; record and compare times and durations in seconds, minutes and hours
evidence: Read 7:43 from an analogue clock face and write it on a digital display
Estimate whether brushing teeth takes about 2 seconds, 2 minutes or 2 hours, then time it to check
Compare 1 minute 20 seconds with 75 seconds and say which is longer
before.assessmentPrompt: If the kitchen clock shows 7:43, can {{name}} read the exact time and write it as it would look on a digital clock — and say which is longer, 1 minute 20 seconds or 75 seconds?

after.name: Time to the nearest minute
after.description: Read and write time to the nearest minute on analogue and digital clocks. Coordinate the minute scale with the hour hand, and express equivalent minutes-past and minutes-to readings.
evidence: Read 7:43 from an analogue clock face and write it on a digital display, keeping the hour as 7 although the hour hand is near 8
Read an analogue clock showing 11:06, explaining why the hour hand is just past 11 and the minute hand is six minutes past the hour
Express 9:57 as three minutes to ten and explain the hour-hand position
after.assessmentPrompt: If an analogue kitchen clock shows 7:43, can {{name}} read and write the time and explain why the hour is still 7? On another clock showing 9:57, can they write the digital time and say how many minutes remain until ten?

evidence: Use a sand timer or stopwatch to time an activity

Compare the duration of two activities (e.g. 'the race took longer than the walk')
Sequence intervals on a timeline
before.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} knows a film takes 2 hours and a car journey takes 45 minutes, can they tell you which takes longer — and put a few daily activities in order of how long they take?

after.name: Comparing and ordering durations
after.description: Compare and sequence intervals of time
evidence: Order three events by how long they took
Compare the duration of two activities (e.g. 'the race took longer than the walk')
Sequence intervals on a timeline
Compare a 35-minute bus journey with a 40-minute walk and say which takes longer and by how much
Compare 1 minute 20 seconds with 75 seconds by expressing them in a common unit
after.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is given durations of 35 minutes, 40 minutes and 25 minutes, can they order them and say how much longer 40 minutes is than 35? Can they compare 1 minute 20 seconds with 75 seconds and explain why finishing later alone does not show a longer duration?

before.name: Roman numeral and 24-hour clocks
before.description: Tell and write the time from analogue clocks with Roman-numeral faces (I to XII, including IV, which some clocks show as IIII, and IX), knowing that the minute positions are the same as on a clock with ordinary numbers; and read and write times on 12-hour and 24-hour clocks, knowing that the 24-hour clock runs from 00:00 at midnight to 23:59. Times from 1:00 a.m. to 11:59 a.m. keep the same hour (7:05 a.m. = 07:05); times from 1:00 p.m. to 11:59 p.m. are 12 hours more (3:20 p.m. = 15:20). The 12 o'clock hour is the exception to both: 12:20 p.m., just after noon, stays 12:20, and 12:20 a.m., just after midnight, becomes 00:20. Fluent conversion between 12- and 24-hour times is developed in Year 4
evidence: Read a Roman-numeral clock with the minute hand on IX and the hour hand between IV and V as quarter to five (4:45)
Match the Roman numerals I to XII to the hour positions on a blank clock face, including IV (or IIII), IX and XII
Write 3:20 p.m. as 15:20 and 7:05 a.m. as 07:05, then write 12:20 p.m. as 12:20 and 12:20 a.m. as 00:20, explaining why adding 12 works only for p.m. times from 1 p.m. onwards
before.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a clock with Roman numerals where the minute hand points to IX and the hour hand is between IV and V, can they read it as quarter to five — and say what time 15:20 on a 24-hour clock means?

after.name: Roman-numeral clock faces
after.description: Tell and write the time from analogue clocks with Roman-numeral faces I to XII, including IV (also shown as IIII on some clocks) and IX. Interpret the numeral positions and hands as on an ordinary numbered clock face.
evidence: Read a Roman-numeral clock with the minute hand on IX and the hour hand between IV and V as quarter to five (4:45)
Match I to XII to hour positions on a clock face, including IV or IIII, IX and XII
Read the same hand positions on Roman and ordinary numbered clock faces, explaining that changing numeral labels does not change the time
after.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a Roman-numeral clock with the minute hand on IX and the hour hand between IV and V, can they read it as quarter to five and explain whether a clock labelled IIII instead of IV would show a different time?

before.name: 12-hour and 24-hour time
before.description: Read, write, and convert time between analogue and digital 12-hour and 24-hour clocks
evidence: Convert 3:45 pm to 15:45 in 24-hour time
Read 19:30 and state the 12-hour equivalent as 7:30 pm
Match a set of 12-hour and 24-hour times
before.assessmentPrompt: If a train timetable shows a departure at 14:35, can {{name}} convert that to 12-hour clock time — and tell you whether that's morning or afternoon?

after.name: 12-hour and 24-hour time
after.description: Read, write and convert time between ordinary analogue and digital 12-hour and 24-hour clocks. Morning hours 1–11 keep their hour (7:05 a.m. = 07:05); afternoon/evening hours 1–11 add 12 (3:20 p.m. = 15:20). The 12 o’clock hour has separate noon and midnight cases: 12:20 p.m. = 12:20 and 12:20 a.m. = 00:20. Convert in both directions without requiring Roman-numeral clock faces.
evidence: Convert 3:45 pm to 15:45 in 24-hour time
Read 19:30 and state the 12-hour equivalent as 7:30 pm
Match a set of 12-hour and 24-hour times
Convert 12:20 a.m. to 00:20 and 12:20 p.m. to 12:20, explaining the midnight and noon cases
Read an ordinary analogue clock with a stated afternoon context and write the equivalent 24-hour digital time; translate back to a 12-hour display
after.assessmentPrompt: If a train leaves at 14:35, can {{name}} give the 12-hour time and part of the day, then write 12:20 a.m. and 12:20 p.m. in 24-hour time? Can they also translate a stated afternoon time on an ordinary analogue clock?

before.name: Time Units and Calendar Facts
before.description: Know the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year, and leap year
evidence: State that there are 60 seconds in a minute
Name the months and state the number of days in each
Explain that a leap year has 366 days and occurs every 4 years
before.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} how many days are in September and whether this year is a leap year, can they answer both — and tell you how many seconds are in a minute?

after.name: Time Units and Calendar Facts
after.description: Know the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year, and leap year
evidence: State that there are 60 seconds in a minute
Name the months and state the number of days in each
Explain that a leap year has 366 days; leap years usually follow a four-year pattern, with calendar exceptions, so check a calendar for a particular year
after.assessmentPrompt: If you give {{name}} a calendar, can they say how many days are in September and whether that year has 365 or 366 days, and tell you how many seconds are in a minute?

Use 'earlier' and 'later' correctly to describe daily events
Solve practical problems like 'Who finished first?'
before.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} finishes their dinner before a sibling, can they tell you who finished earlier — and which one was quicker?

after.name: Time comparison words
after.description: Use comparative language for time: quicker, slower, earlier, later
evidence: Compare two events and say which was quicker/slower
Use 'earlier' and 'later' correctly to describe daily events
Solve practical problems like 'Who finished first?'
